newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries steady in London post rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries steady in London post rate rise.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were steady in London on Wednesday as the dust settled on Tuesday's 25 basis point U.S. interest rate hike.
But traders said a growing belief that more rate rises are in the pipeline would prompt the long bond to test the critical 7.0 percent yield near term.
"There are a few buyers on weakness around, but their number has diminished considerably now the rate change has been made official," said Charles Quigley, vice-president at Chase here.
"I have no doubt there are much better profit takers around should prices rise from here."
By 1121 GMT the 30-year benchmark bond was at 95-22 to yield 6.97 percent. The bond closed at 95-20 bid in Tokyo and 95-23 bid in New York.

Quigley said trade was fairly subdued. "This was one of the most well advertised policy changes in the history of the Fed so it wasn't a huge shock, but some people still need to tidy up between now and the end of tomorrow."
The U.S. market is on holiday on Friday.

"I don't think we have the luxury of waiting in this environment. If the Fed is really serious about slowing the economy down, certainly 25 basis points is just the beginning as it's not enough to affect an economy the size of the U.S.," said Quigley.
Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica in London, agreed Tuesday's rate rise signalled the beginning of a series in the U.S.

"I am negative on the Treasury market, but not hugely," he said. "It's difficult to believe the Fed will want to tighten aggressively -- I don't think we'll see a big upswing in interest rates," he said.
Analysts said the market would turn its attention firmly to real side data now, in particular next Friday's labour report.
Quigley said the possibility of a weak payrolls number may prompt a short covering rally into next week.
"If the market sells off much further, we might see the beginnings of a short covering rally next week. People may want to be closer to even going into the report."
June T-bond futures were at 108-23, unchanged from the previous close in Chicago.
